name: Citizenship by Registration -- Minor Dependants

qualifying_event.description: A minor (under 18) may be registered as a citizen on application by their 'responsible parent' or guardian.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Child's birth certificate; proof of the responsible parent's identity/custody status.

requirements.blocker_text: Route applies to minors (persons under 18 years).
Application must be made by the 'responsible parent' -- defined as the father, OR, where the father is dead or a court has awarded custody to the mother, the mother.

evidence_required.document: Proof of the responsible parent's identity and (where relevant) custody order or father's death certificate

sources.title: Grenada Citizenship Act, Cap 54, Section 6(1) (primary legislation): registration of minors on application by the 'responsible parent' -- defined as the father, or the mother where the father is dead or has lost custody by court order

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Grenada's initial build. IMPORTANT, well-documented gender asymmetry confirmed directly from the primary Act text: the 'responsible parent' who may apply for a minor's registration defaults to the FATHER -- the mother gains that standing only if the father is dead or a court has specifically awarded her custody. This is a materially different (and more father-favouring) default than the gender-neutral constitutional descent rule in gd_citizenship_by_descent.json (Section 97, which lets either parent transmit citizenship automatically to a child born abroad) -- this registration route instead concerns WHO may apply on a minor's behalf, a distinct administrative gatekeeping question from whose citizenship the child inherits. Flagged prominently rather than smoothed over, consistent with how gender-asymmetric rules were flagged for the Bahamas earlier this session.
